# gns3_suspend_nodes (Action)

Sends suspend to GNS3 nodes in one project. Without `node_ids` it makes one `POST /v2/projects/{project_id}/nodes/suspend` call for every node in the project; with `node_ids` it makes one `POST /v2/projects/{project_id}/nodes/{node_id}/suspend` call per node, in sorted order, and stops at the first error. The action changes no state and has no outputs.

Actions need Terraform 1.14 or later. Invoke it from a resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` block or with `terraform apply -invoke=action.gns3_suspend_nodes.<name>`.

VPCS has no suspend: GNS3 2.2.61 accepts the call and the node keeps running (see `docs/api-drift.md`, "Node actions and snapshots (2.2.61)"). After the call the action re-reads each targeted node and warns about any whose status did not change.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Actions need Terraform 1.14 or later.
resource "gns3_project" "lab" {
  name = "tf-example-suspend-nodes"
}

data "gns3_template" "vpcs" {
  name = "VPCS"
}

resource "gns3_node" "pc1" {
  project_id  = gns3_project.lab.project_id
  template_id = data.gns3_template.vpcs.template_id
  name        = "PC1"

  # Suspend every node in the project after this node is changed.
  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_update]
      actions = [action.gns3_suspend_nodes.all]
    }
  }
}

# No node_ids: every node in the project.
action "gns3_suspend_nodes" "all" {
  config {
    project_id = gns3_project.lab.project_id
  }
}

# Only the nodes named. Run it on demand:
# terraform apply -invoke=action.gns3_suspend_nodes.pc1
action "gns3_suspend_nodes" "pc1" {
  config {
    project_id = gns3_project.lab.project_id
    node_ids   = [gns3_node.pc1.node_id]
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) ID of the project whose nodes to suspend. The project must be open.

### Optional

- `node_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the nodes to suspend. Null or empty means every node in the project, through the project-wide endpoint.
